Find gene orthologs

Source: R/orthologs.R
orthologs.Rd

Find cross-species orthologs for a set of genes.

Usage

orthologs(
  genes,
  source,
  target,
  synonyms = TRUE,
  best = TRUE,
  min_support = 1,
  orthologs_only = TRUE
)

Arguments

genes

A character vector of gene symbols or NCBI/Ensembl gene IDs (case-sensitive).

source

Species of genes, such as "mouse". See species().

target

Species in which to find orthologs.

synonyms

If TRUE (default), check gene synonyms for inputs with no direct match.

best

If TRUE (default), keep only the best matches, which can differ between search directions.

min_support

Minimum number of methods or sources that support a gene pair. Use one positive whole number. The maximum possible count depends on the species pair.

orthologs_only

If TRUE (default), keep only inputs with at least one matching pair.

Value

A data frame with one row per distinct input and matching gene pair, in input order. With orthologs_only = FALSE, each distinct nonmissing input with no matching pair gets one row with its value in input and NA in all other columns.

Details

The function uses each distinct input once. Different inputs for the same gene each get their own rows. A valid gene can have no known orthologs in the data.

The source AGR dataset includes orthologs from multiple sources, such as PANTHER, SonicParanoid, and OrthoFinder. For pairs supported by three or more methods, a best match in either direction is sufficient for the AGR stringent set. For pairs supported by two methods, a best match in both directions is required. The set also includes all pairs from ZFIN or HGNC.

References

Alliance of Genome Resources Consortium. Updates to the Alliance of Genome Resources central infrastructure. Genetics. 2024. doi: doi:10.1093/genetics/iyae049 .

Examples

orthologs(genes = "TP53", source = "human", target = "mouse")
#>   input source_taxon_id source_symbol source_ncbi_id source_ensembl_id
#> 1  TP53            9606          TP53           7157   ENSG00000141510
#>   target_taxon_id target_symbol target_ncbi_id  target_ensembl_id
#> 1           10090         Trp53          22059 ENSMUSG00000059552
#>                                                                                    support
#> 1 HGNC|Hieranoid|InParanoid|OMA|OrthoFinder|OrthoInspector|PANTHER|PhylomeDB|SonicParanoid
#>   support_n
#> 1         9
orthologs(genes = c("Ptprc", "Cd34"), source = "mouse", target = "human")
#>   input source_taxon_id source_symbol source_ncbi_id  source_ensembl_id
#> 1 Ptprc           10090         Ptprc          19264 ENSMUSG00000026395
#> 2  Cd34           10090          Cd34          12490 ENSMUSG00000016494
#>   target_taxon_id target_symbol target_ncbi_id target_ensembl_id
#> 1            9606         PTPRC           5788   ENSG00000081237
#> 2            9606          CD34            947   ENSG00000174059
#>                                                                                                    support
#> 1 Ensembl Compara|HGNC|Hieranoid|InParanoid|OMA|OrthoFinder|OrthoInspector|PANTHER|PhylomeDB|SonicParanoid
#> 2 Ensembl Compara|HGNC|Hieranoid|InParanoid|OMA|OrthoFinder|OrthoInspector|PANTHER|PhylomeDB|SonicParanoid
#>   support_n
#> 1        10
#> 2        10
orthologs(genes = "Trp53", source = "mouse", target = "rat")
#>   input source_taxon_id source_symbol source_ncbi_id  source_ensembl_id
#> 1 Trp53           10090         Trp53          22059 ENSMUSG00000059552
#>   target_taxon_id target_symbol target_ncbi_id  target_ensembl_id
#> 1           10116          Tp53          24842 ENSRNOG00000010756
#>                                                                                               support
#> 1 Ensembl Compara|Hieranoid|InParanoid|OMA|OrthoFinder|OrthoInspector|PANTHER|PhylomeDB|SonicParanoid
#>   support_n
#> 1         9
